newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees A$3.85 bln budget deficit in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees A$3.85 bln budget deficit in 97/98.

text.p: The Australian government said in its budget on Tuesday it expected an underlying budget deficit of A$3.853 billion in the year ended June 30, 199 of A$6.856 billion.
Economists had forecast a underlying deficit for 1997/98 of around A$2 billion.

Treasury officials said the government's effective starting point deficit for this year's budget process was A$4.205 billion, well above the A$3.926 billion deficit starting point released by the government in January and also above the A$3.8 billion level forecast by many economists.
The starting point deficit is the Treasury's estimate of what the budget outcome would be without any policy change and includes the budget effects of Treasury's latest economic forecasts.

The government said the net or real improvement to the budget deficit from its budget decisions in 1997/98 would be A$352 million, well below the A$1 billion to A$2 billion in real deficit cuts many economists had forecast.
The government forecast its underlying budget would be A$1.597 billion in surplus by 1998/99, rising to a surplus of A$5.383 billion in 1999/00 and A$10.692 billion in 2000/01.

The government said it forecast a headline surplus of A$6.423 billion in 1997/98, up from a surplus of A$764 million in 1996/97. These surpluses are due to hefty asset sales already announced and, in some cases, completed.

This headline surplus, which includes asset sales proceeds and early state debt repayments, was expected to rise to A$6.784 billion in 1998/99, A$5.777 billion in 1999/00 and A$11.096 billion in 2000/01.

The government said its 1997/98 budget policy measures would lead to real improvements in the underlying budget position of A$1.941 billion in 1998/99 and an improvement of A$2.011 billion in 1999/00.
